You go back to the barracks like any tired man and lie rigid until the second bell. This time the greataxe goes on your back, Dargan's sash against your spine, and a torch from your pack rides in your fist. Pip snores under his cap. You ease the door shut behind you.

Inside, through the barred window, you can see the lamp, the night scribe half-risen from his stool, and the shelf with the copy of the ledger. Up the slope the alarm bell goes on. You have seconds before the whole mine wakes.

You have him by the collar before the pen finishes falling, and you bellow it right into his face: sit quiet and live. His eyes go very wide. He nods and keeps nodding. You bind his wrists and ankles with his own sash and gag him with his sleeve-cuff, and he doesn't struggle.

The copy ledger is on the shelf behind the desk, a fat book bound in tin-backed leather, with neat columns of names and dates, children's names among them, over and over. You hold it to the lamp. Above you the third gate is a black notch against the red glow, where a sister is waiting at the wash-house door for the second bell.

You get them up one hand at a time. The smallest ride on bigger backs, and a girl of five rides on yours, her chin on your helmless head. You get them up, and they come. Ninna passes the word down the line, and the children cross the stream in knots of ten with the big ones carrying the small. You wade the rear with the shield on your arm. On the far bank the high road runs south, pale and rutted. For three hours you walk it, with the sun climbing and the children's feet dragging. Twice you take a tired one onto your back. The grey shape on the ridge falls farther behind and then is gone.

Tessa went ahead hooded and quick, and she is back before noon, running low along the verge. She doesn't slow until she reaches you.

"Vael," she says, breathless. "Two miles north-east, where the road comes down from Cinder Ford. He's mounted, with thirty hobgoblins behind him in column, banners up, the full Tallies. They're not hurrying. They've seen the dust." She wipes her mouth. "Sergeant Ushk is at his stirrup. I couldn't see the mask's face. I couldn't see Brakk."

The road here crosses a long open shelf of grass, with a dry wall of tumbled stone along one side and nothing else for a mile. The children are strung out on it behind you, ninety-four of them, with no cover that would hide them from thirty soldiers.

It is a little past noon. You are at 5 hit points with a longsword, a shield, and a breath that will warm one cone of hobgoblins. Your oath is to Vael. Your sister is at your elbow, and the children are at your back.

sheet.name: Korvash Emberhide
sheet.opening: Korvash Emberhide, a hulking red-scaled dragonborn barbarian (Chaotic Good, loud, proud, quick to anger; ideal Charity; bond: he keeps his word no matter what; flaw: inflexible), arrives at dusk in a lowland market town near the foot of the mountains, driving off a pack of bullies shaking down a family of herders, as he has done for years. His past, which the opening must respect: he comes from a clan of mountain herders. When he was young, hobgoblins of the Iron Tallies warband, led by a tin-masked captain named Gorrak Vael (who notches a rod for every raid), overran his village. His father Dargan held the narrow Goat's Throat pass, losing a hand and then his life, so the herd and the children could flee; Korvash swore to him, with his blood on his hands, to protect the weak. His younger sister Tessa was lost in the raid and her fate is UNKNOWN: he never saw her fall and has never stopped wondering, so she must not be confirmed alive or dead unless discovered in play. The survivors fled to Harrowmere, where his aunt Veshra raised him and still sends word by travelers. The clan built a cairn at the Goat's Throat, which he has never had the heart to revisit. His shame at being too young to stand beside his father is why he is loud and makes sure everyone knows he is standing. He carries his father's second-best greataxe with Dargan's ember-red scale-sash tied to the haft. Hook for the opening: just after the bullies flee, a frightened young herder or a traveler brings him word, perhaps carried from Aunt Veshra, that a hobgoblin warband bearing a tin-masked captain and a notched rod has been seen again, or that something connected to the Goat's Throat has turned up. This pulls him toward an oath-bound choice: someone weak is in immediate danger, he promises to help, and keeping that word will lead him back toward the mountains and the questions about Tessa. Invent only original places and people; keep it grounded in the SRD's monsters (hobgoblins, goblins, bugbears, wolves, etc.).

Those who share your religion will support you (but only you) at a modest lifestyle. This could be the temple where you used to serve, if you remain on good terms with it, or a temple where you have found a new home. While near your temple, you can call upon the priests for assistance, provided the assistance you ask for is not hazardous and you remain in good standing with your temple.

line:
The rest is done and every hour nearer Greyshaft's hounds is an hour wasted, so I get the column on its feet. "Up, little ones, we cross here and take the high road home, and anyone too tired rides on my back."

I send Tessa ahead along the road hooded and quick to scout for Vael's column, and I walk the rear with the shield on my arm and my breath weapon ready, so that if Gorrak arrives it's on the open road with the children well behind me.

input.add_to_description: Day 19 ~12:10 PM: column crossed the stream and took the high road south; Korvash 5 HP, breath weapon ready, Rage spent. Tessa scouted ahead unseen (19) and saw an Iron Tallies column marching north on the road beyond a wooded rise, about two miles ahead: about thirty hobgoblins, with Gorrak Vael's tin mask at the head and Sergeant Ushk beside him; no Brakk seen. They are marching to Greyshaft at speed and have not yet seen the children. Grey scouts still shadow from behind.

You get the column up with a growl and a few gentle hands, and the children cross the stream in a long wet line, the little ones riding the big ones, two on your own back. By the time the sun stands high you are a mile down the high road. You walk the rear with the shield on your arm and your breath banked, and the grey shape on the ridge keeps pace behind you.

Tessa goes ahead as you told her, hooded, quick and silent, and you lose sight of her within a hundred paces. She is gone for most of two hours. She comes back low through the roadside brush, breathing hard, and drops beside you so that only you hear.

"Two miles on, past the wooded rise. A column marching north, close order. Thirty hobgoblins, near enough, with shields and packs." Her mouth is tight. "A tin mask at the head. Ushk walks beside him, the sergeant from the cairn. I didn't see Brakk." She swallows. "They're coming fast. They haven't seen us, but the road is the only road here, and the grey cloaks behind will whistle the moment they do."

It is just past noon. The column of children is strung out on the open road behind you, with fields on one side and a steep wooded bank on the other. There's no time to hide ninety-four children, but a hollow in the wood might hide them for a little while. Or you can walk down the road to meet the man you swore to answer to. You have 5 hit points, your breath weapon and a shield, and Gorrak Vael is two miles off.
